# Halo Mega Bloks (Project Haggar) decompilation

> Decompilation and native PC port of Project Haggar, the cancelled Halo Mega Bloks game (n-Space, Xbox 360, Unreal Engine 3). Also spelled "Halo Mega Blocks". n-Space built it on the UDK July 2012 BETA 2 engine until 343 Industries cancelled it in 2013. The project rebuilds a development build from source: a static recompilation of the whole Xbox 360 executable for a native port (PC first, then an Anbernic handheld), a byte-matching decompilation of n-Space's own C++, and the game's UnrealScript. Source only, released under CC0 1.0; no game files or SDK files are included, and users supply their own copy of the build.

## Key facts

- Game: Project Haggar, the Halo Mega Bloks game by n-Space for the Xbox 360, cancelled in 2013. Engine: Unreal Engine 3, exactly UDK July 2012 BETA 2 (engine version 10246, changelist 1340247).
- Inputs: a development build with a full private PDB (237,168 functions, 759,808 type records). The executable is a devkit-signed XEX2.
- Matching compiler: XDK 21076, cl 16.00.11886 for PowerPC, with each object's command line from the PDB. 1,258 n-Space functions in scope, 8 of them matched (10 matched in total).
- Port: the recompiled build runs natively on Windows x86-64 from boot to the first level (ReXGlue SDK codegen and its Xenia-derived runtime; 237,162 functions, no unimplemented instruction), and builds on Linux. Next: Linux on real GPUs, then a native renderer for handhelds.
- Scripts: 758 UnrealScript classes (n-Space's own and those modified from UDK) are in script/.
- Not playable natively yet.
